elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: New Section 11.7: "each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed..." — symmetrical by its terms, and no retained sentence states either Party's liability is unlimited.

elements.element: The cap is the greater of fees paid or payable in the 12 months preceding the claim and USD 1,000,000.
elements.evidence: Section 11.7 states only "the fees paid or payable by AbbVie under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim"; no USD 1,000,000 floor and no "greater of" construction is volunteered (the comment concedes this).

elements.element: The exclusion of indirect and consequential damages applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Retained Section 11.5: "NEITHER PARTY NOR ANY OF ITS AFFILIATES SHALL BE LIABLE FOR INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, SPECIAL, EXEMPLARY, PUNITIVE OR CONSEQUENTIAL DAMAGES" — mutual and left verbatim.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Section 11.7 excepts "a Party's breach of its obligations under Article 9 or Section 5.8"; Article 9 is the confidentiality Article referenced in the same capacity by retained Section 11.5.

elements.element: Breach of data protection and security obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: Section 11.7 carves out only fraud/wilful misconduct/gross negligence, Article 9, Section 5.8 and Article 11 indemnities; no data protection or security obligation is placed outside the cap.
Section 11.7 excepts "a Party's indemnification obligations under this Article 11", which covers the mutual indemnities in Sections 11.1 and 11.2.
Section 11.7: "Except for a Party's fraud, willful misconduct or gross negligence..."
Section 11.7 expressly excepts "willful misconduct" from the cap for either Party.

elements.element: Infringement of the other party's intellectual property is uncapped.
elements.evidence: No IP-infringement carve-out appears in Section 11.7; the drafter only says in the rationale that it "would also press" for it — a promise in the comment, not operative language.

elements.element: Customer payment obligations are excluded from damages subject to the cap.
elements.evidence: Section 11.7 caps "total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement" with no exclusion for AbbVie's Article 6 upfront/option, milestone and royalty payment obligations.

elements.element: The aggregate liability cap applies mutually to both parties.
elements.evidence: Section 11.7 applies to "each Party's total aggregate liability"; Harpoon and AbbVie are treated identically.

elements.element: The cap is based on 12 months of fees.
elements.evidence: Section 11.7 fixes the cap at "the fees paid or payable by AbbVie under this Agreement in the twelve (12) months preceding the claim" — a 12-month fee basis on its face (see reasons for the undefined-"fees" risk).
"a Party's indemnification obligations under this Article 11" is expressly outside the cap.

elements.element: Breach of confidentiality obligations is uncapped.
elements.evidence: "a Party's breach of its obligations under Article 9" is expressly outside the cap, mirroring retained Section 11.5(B).
Section 11.7 opening exception expressly includes gross negligence.
Section 11.7 opening exception expressly includes willful misconduct.

reasons: Fallback is complete: a single inserted Section 11.7 delivers a mutual cap on a 12-month fee basis with indemnification, confidentiality (Article 9), gross negligence and wilful misconduct expressly outside the cap. No level-complete element is left to the margin comment.

Preferred fails on four elements: (i) no "greater of ... and USD 1,000,000" floor; (ii) no carve-out for breach of data protection/security obligations; (iii) no carve-out for infringement of the other Party's intellectual property; (iv) no statement that AbbVie's payment obligations are not damages subject to the cap. To move to preferred, amend 11.7 to read "...shall not exceed the greater of (a) the fees paid or payable by AbbVie ... in the twelve (12) months immediately preceding the event giving rise to the claim and (b) USD 1,000,000" and add the missing carve-outs plus "AbbVie's obligation to pay amounts due under Article 6 shall not be subject to this cap."

Substantive defect in the cap basis even at fallback: "fees" is not a defined term in this Agreement and the consideration is an upfront/option payment, Article 6 milestones and Net Sales royalties. As drafted the cap could be read as near-zero in any 12-month window without a "fee" payment, making Harpoon's exposure to AbbVie illusory. Repair by using "all amounts paid or payable by AbbVie under this Agreement" (or an express reference to Article 6 payments) and, preferably, adding the USD 1,000,000 floor.

Related repair: because 11.7 caps "total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement", it is capable of being read against AbbVie's own retained Article 6 payment obligations. This is not a facial contradiction (caps and debt obligations customarily coexist), but the payment carve-out named above should be added to remove the ambiguity against retained royalty/milestone mechanics.

Minimality holds: one concise new section at the end of Article 11, Section 11.5 left verbatim, no renumbering of 11.6, no survival tail, procedure or extra damages categories. The fraud and Section 5.8 carve-outs are not gratuitous extras — they mirror retained Section 11.5(A)-(B) and are needed so the new cap does not swallow exposures that are presently uncapped.

Intent preserved: the mutual indirect/consequential exclusion, the mutual indemnities, the insurance minimums and the Article 6 payment ceilings survive; the new cross-references (Article 9, Section 5.8, Article 11) all resolve and no dangling reference is created.

Commercial caution for the deal team (consistent with the drafter's note): the pre-existing regime is mutually uncapped, which is not a walk-away outcome and preserves AbbVie's full recourse against Harpoon. Introducing any cap trades that recourse away, so this edit should be raised only if the business wants symmetry; severity is downgraded accordingly.
